thirty_second.text: Agent-Reach is an MIT-licensed Python command-line tool that lets AI agents read and search sites such as Twitter/X, Reddit, YouTube, GitHub, Bilibili and XiaoHongShu without paid APIs. It chains free tools like yt-dlp, the gh CLI, feedparser, Jina Reader and Exa. Users install it by pasting a one-line prompt that points their agent to an install.md file. Created on February 24, 2026, it had 95,358 stars, 8,341 forks and 36 contributors by October 10, 2026, with most growth arriving in three short bursts that overlapped with GitHub Trending placements.

origin.text: The repository was created on February 24, 2026, and its first release, v1.1.0, came out the next day, adding Instagram, LinkedIn and Boss直聘. Its stated purpose is to give AI agents access to the internet. The maintainer says he uses the tool daily and will keep maintaining it. The sources do not explain why he started it beyond that stated purpose.

flywheel.text: The clearest repeating pattern is GitHub Trending visibility. Agent-Reach first appeared in trending rankings on June 5, 2026, at #3 in Python. It reached #1 on June 15 and stayed on trending for 32 days. In early October it ranked #1 across all languages on October 2, and #3 overall and #1 in Python on Trendshift from October 2–4. Each of these stretches overlaps with a large star burst: about 20,000 stars from June 5–25 and about 7,700 from October 2–9. This fits a loop in which trending placement shows the repo to more developers and their stars keep it ranked. The sources record the overlap in timing, but none of them states that one caused the other.

did_differently.text: Interpretation: rather than writing its own scrapers, the project presents itself as a capability layer that selects, installs, health-checks and routes to existing free tools. Each platform is a channel with an ordered list of backends. When Bilibili blocked yt-dlp, the tool switched to bili-cli without users rewriting their skills. Sources disagree on when this happened: most say June 2026, one says March. An 'agent-reach doctor' command reports which routes currently work. Installation is handed to the user's AI agent through an install.md prompt. The tool is also offered as an agent skill (npx skills add) and as a pip package, and it has READMEs in four languages plus a China mirror on AtomGit. The v1.4.2 and v1.5.0 releases in June removed unmaintained channels and added multi-backend routing.

key_takeaways.text: Star growth was uneven and arrived in bursts. The repo gained 9,240 stars in its first three weeks, about 20,000 in June 5–25 and about 7,700 in October 2–9. After each of the first two bursts, the daily pace stayed well above the pace beforehand.

Hacker News played a small role in what is visible. Two August 2026 posts drew 1–4 points, and one outlet described the appearance as a low-engagement signal. This suggests the attention came through other channels, with GitHub Trending the best documented.
Letting the user's own AI agent run the installation may lower setup effort for the intended audience. The evidence shows the method was used, not how much it affected adoption.

Because the tool depends on scrapers, it is fragile. The project handles this with backend fallbacks and a health-check command. Outside reviewers still note terms-of-service risk, breakage when sites patch, channels that need logins, and no test suite.

Reported figures vary a lot between sources. Third-party star counts range from 31K to 95K depending on capture date, and one source says no GitHub release was published while GitHub itself shows seven. A SitePoint tutorial warned its code might be illustrative. These numbers should be checked against primary data before relying on them.
